catalog_quote: [Foreman & Marten 1973, 4.3.1, p.99:] Tone and length are not phonemically pertinent. Stress is predictable and, therefore, non-phonemic. The following rules apply to the placement of stress on the word level. 1. The first syllable of a word which contains /a/ is stressed. 2. When there is no syllable containing /a/ in a word, the first syllable of the word is stressed. /amʌᵐbʌ/ ('amʌᵐbʌ) 'running' /tʌwknaᵐbʌ/ ('tʰowk'naᵐbʌ) 'sleeping' /sɨᵽa/ (sɨ'ᵽa) 'seed' /wɔřamsɨ/ (wɒ'ramsɨ) 'tobacco' /tɨtɨtɨ/ ('tʰɨtɨtɨ) 'will stand' /lʌwsɨ/ ('lowsɨ) 'tongs' ... [OPD 2004, Suprasegmentals:] In a word, either the first syllable or the first syllable containing /ɑ/ is stressed. ... [Marten 1995, 5:] On the word level either the first syllable or the syllable containing the phoneme /a/ is stressed. There is no tone or length.

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: Quote check: the deciding 1973 passage and both later restatements are verbatim in held page images/scanned at the stated locators. Deciding source is the dedicated SIL phonemic statement (1973) by the language's principal describers, with explicit rules and stress-marked examples; a 1978 revision of the same paper (SIL archives 31302, downloaded now via the Internet Archive, scanned p.25) repeats the two rules word for word with re-transcribed examples, and the 1995 and 2004 documents agree. Glottolog's bibliography contains no competing or later phonological description; the only unheld substantial work is Foreman's own 1974 grammar, available only via controlled lending, which is unlikely to change a SEGMENTAL-OTHER (leftmost /a/, else initial) coding.org full-catalog search, and the the Internet Archive

sources.quote: 'Tone and length are not phonemically pertinent. Stress is predictable, and therefore, non-phonemic. The following rules apply to the placement of stress on the word level. 1. The first syllable of a word which contains /a/ is stressed. 2. When there is no syllable containing /a/ in a word, the first syllable of the word is stressed.' Examples re-transcribed in a revised vowel orthography: ('ameᵐbʌ) 'running', (tʰɔk'naᵐbʌ) 'sleeping', (si'ᵽa) 'seed', (wu'řamse) 'tobacco', ('tʰetete) 'will stand', ('lowsi) 'tongs'.
